title: Case Statements
story: case matches a word against patterns. It is tidier than a long if-elif chain.
goal: Print the kind of the first argument: ending in .py is python, .sh is shell, .md is docs, anything else is other.
hints: Patterns like *.py end with ) and each branch ends with ;;
The last pattern *) catches everything else.
socratic: How would you match two patterns in one branch?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Case Statements”?
